articles.title: Amelioration of Oxidative Stress in Melanocytes by Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Exosomes via the Keap1-Nrf2 Axis.
articles.abstract: Oxidative stress, particularly H₂O₂ accumulation, is a key pathogenic factor in vitiligo, yet therapies that directly protect melanocytes remain limited. Adipose-derived stem cell-derived exosomes (ADSC-Exos) are cell-free vesicles with reported antioxidant effects, but whether they act through the Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)-nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway is unknown. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of ADSC-Exos on hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂)-induced oxidative damage in human melanocytes and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, focusing on the Keap1-Nrf2 signaling pathway. ADSCs and their exosomes were isolated and characterized using flow cytometry, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), and western blot. An oxidative stress model was established by treating PIG1 human melanocytes with H₂O₂. The therapeutic effects of ADSC-Exos were assessed by measuring cell viability, migration, intracellular ROS levels, DNA damage, and antioxidant enzyme activities. The involvement of the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway was examined by western blot and immunofluorescence. H₂O₂ treatment significantly induced oxidative stress in PIG1 cells, evidenced by reduced cell viability and migration, increased ROS accumulation, and elevated DNA damage. Treatment with ADSC-Exos markedly restored cellular functions. Mechanistically, ADSC-Exos downregulated the expression of Keap1, facilitated the nuclear translocation of Nrf2, and upregulated the expression of downstream antioxidant enzymes, including heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). The findings demonstrate that ADSC-Exos effectively ameliorate H₂O₂-induced oxidative damage in melanocytes. The cytoprotection is mediated through the activation of the Keap1-Nrf2-ARE signaling pathway. These findings support further investigation of ADSC-Exos as a potential therapeutic strategy for vitiligo.

articles.title: Dual-Modal Sensing of Enantiomeric Purity Using Chiral Au@CuxS Nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Enantiomeric discrimination is essential for a range of pharmacological and biochemical applications. Herein, we present a rational design of chiral Au@CuxS nanoparticles (NPs) that serve as a dual-modal sensing platform for determining enantiomeric purity. By synergizing the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of the Au core with the semiconducting properties of the CuxS shell, these NPs exhibit robust chiroptical activity alongside enhanced near-infrared (NIR)-responsive photocatalytic and photothermal performances. We demonstrate that enantioselective interactions between target chiral analytes with antioxidant capabilities, such as glutathione (GSH), tryptophan (Trp), aspartic acid (Asp), and cysteine (Cys), and the NP surfaces serve as mechanisms to modulate reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and photothermal conversion. Specifically, the catalytic degradation of chromogenic substrates and the concomitant temperature increase are highly sensitive to the enantiomeric ratios of these analytes, which act as interfacial modulators. This dual-signal strategy enables rapid and accurate chiral discrimination in enantiomeric matrices, providing a versatile analytical platform and highlighting the potential of chiral plasmonic-semiconductor heterostructures in precise molecular recognition.

articles.title: Cystine-Dependent Redox Metabolism Determines Photodynamic Therapy Response in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains difficult to treat without substantial functional and cosmetic morbidity, as current management relies largely on surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy. However, these approaches often fail to achieve effective tumor control in therapy-resistant HNSCC. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has strong potential for HNSCC treatment because it enables spatially restricted tumor ablation while limiting damage to surrounding healthy tissue. Here, we apply a near-infrared (NIR) cyanine-carborate photosensitizer (PS) platform to HNSCC to identify a redox-based mechanism that limits PDT response in resistant cells and evaluate a strategy for sensitizing resistant cells. Using complementary human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive and -negative HNSCC models, we show that PDT induces acute oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation in both sensitive and resistant cells. However, resistant cells counter this stress through an adaptive redox response marked by increased xCT (SLC7A11)-dependent cystine utilization. This response sustains glutathione-linked antioxidant buffering, limits lipid peroxidation, and promotes survival under PDT. Genetic or pharmacologic disruption of cystine uptake prevents this adaptive defense, restores oxidative vulnerability, and sensitizes PDT-resistant HNSCC cells to treatment. Consistent with these mechanistic findings, cyanine-carborate-induced PDT with xCT (SLC7A11) inhibition markedly suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Together, these findings identify xCT-dependent cystine metabolism as a targetable vulnerability for therapeutic sensitization of resistant HNSCC to PDT.

articles.title: The Evolving Landscape of Actinic Keratosis: Field Therapy, New Drugs, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Actinic keratosis (AK) is a dynamic manifestation of chronic ultraviolet injury and a marker of field cancerization, but individual lesions and patients differ substantially in risk. Contemporary management therefore requires lesion-level triage, assessment of field burden, selection of a regimen the patient can complete, and longitudinal prevention rather than a uniform preference for either lesion- or field-directed therapy. This narrative review evaluates advances reported primarily from 2024 through June 2026. Recent evidence supports expanded treatment-area labeling and growing real-world experience with tirbanibulin; indoor and simulated-daylight photodynamic therapy (PDT); laser-assisted PDT; and low-irradiance, abbreviated-incubation, or simultaneous-illumination protocols designed to reduce pain. Short-course topical fluorouracil/calcipotriene has gained mechanistic and expert-consensus support, whereas diclofenac remains a slower and generally less efficacious option for selected patients. Nicotinamide, previously shown to be effective in immunocompetent patients, has not demonstrated benefit in solid organ transplant recipients, and systemic retinoids or capecitabine remain reserved for carefully selected high-risk populations. Senescence-directed glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) modulation, interleukin-1 pathway targets, immune checkpoint blockade, and human papillomavirus vaccination are scientifically important but remain investigational for routine AK prevention. A risk-adapted blended strategy-biopsy when invasion is suspected, lesion-directed treatment for appropriate confirmed AKs, field treatment when subclinical burden is clinically meaningful, and cyclical therapy to aid prevention and provide surveillance for high-risk patients-best reflects current evidence.

articles.title: Hyaluronic acid-based skin booster with glutathione combined with 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser and oral tranexamic acid for melasma: A prospective comparative study.
articles.abstract: Melasma is a chronic, acquired facial hyperpigmentation disorder with multifactorial pathogenesis and frequent relapse. Low-fluence 1064-nm Q-switched neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Nd:YAG) (LQSNY) laser with oral tranexamic acid (TA) is widely used, but responses are often incomplete and short-lived. glutathione (GSH), an antioxidant that inhibits melanogenesis, may improve outcomes when delivered intradermally with a hyaluronic acid (HA) carrier. We assessed whether adding an HA-based GSH skin booster (HA-GSH) to this regimen enhances efficacy and durability. Fifty Chinese women with epidermal melasma (Fitzpatrick III-IV) were randomized 1:1 to 6 monthly LQSNY sessions plus oral TA (250 mg daily), with (Group A) or without (Group B) intradermal HA-GSH. The primary outcome was change in modified melasma area and severity index (mMASI) at 6 months and at 2-month posttreatment follow-up. Secondary outcomes were patient satisfaction (short assessment of patient satisfaction) and safety. Sample size was determined a priori. mMASI was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with baseline mMASI as a covariate and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for visit-level comparisons. Thirty-six patients completed the study (18 per group); baseline mMASI was comparable (5.61 ± 1.29 vs 5.56 ± 1.20; P = .89). Fourteen participants withdrew (seven per group), none due to adverse events. Group A showed significantly greater mMASI reduction from the third session onward. Adjusted for baseline, the mean difference across all post-baseline visits was 0.72 points (95% confidence interval 0.46-0.98; P < .001) favoring Group A, evident at the first posttreatment assessment. At 6 months, mean mMASI was lower in Group A (2.50 ± 0.62 vs 3.39 ± 0.70; P < .001), an advantage maintained at follow-up (2.06 ± 0.54 vs 2.67 ± 0.59; P = .003). More Group A patients were "very satisfied" (28% vs 11%), though not significantly (P = .31). Both regimens were well tolerated; only transient erythema, mild swelling, and bruising occurred, with no serious or pigmentary adverse events. Adding intradermal HA-GSH to LQSNY laser and oral TA produced earlier, greater, and more durable melasma improvement with high satisfaction and a favorable safety profile, supporting HA-GSH as a promising adjuvant pending confirmation in larger, longer trials.

articles.title: Riboflavin as a Regulator of Cellular Metabolism: From the Classic Vitamin B2 to a Key Redox Factor.
articles.abstract: Riboflavin, i.e., vitamin B2, was first isolated by Kuhn and Győrgy in 1933, who reported that it acts as a growth factor. Riboflavin has long been known to play a key role in energy metabolism and cellular respiration, and its deficiency negatively affects skin and mucous membrane health. More recent studies have found it to regulate mitochondrial metabolism and to serve as the core of flavin coenzymes (FAD, FMN), which enable the respiratory chain and β-oxidation. Riboflavin also plays a key role as an antioxidant. While it is not a classic free antioxidant, it supports the enzymatic antioxidant system by supporting glutathione reductase, thioredoxin reductase, and ROS neutralization. On the other hand, when exposed to light, riboflavin exhibits photosensitizing properties that generate reactive oxygen species. As a result, it can initiate oxidative processes involving lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids, thereby exhibiting a prooxidative effect. The aim of this review is to provide an overview of the current understanding of the role of riboflavin in cellular and human health.

articles.title: CWH43 Suppresses Ferroptosis-Associated Vulnerability Through Redox Adaptation in Colorectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death that has emerged as a potential vulnerability in cancer cells under therapeutic stress. However, the mechanisms by which colorectal cancer cells modulate ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of CWH43, a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biogenesis-related protein whose role in chemotherapy response has been unclear, in regulating redox balance and ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer. Integrative analyses of clinical datasets, transcriptomic profiling, and functional experiments were performed using gain- and loss-of-function approaches in CRC cell models. We found that elevated CWH43 expression was associated with adverse clinical outcomes and reduced responsiveness to chemotherapy. Functionally, CWH43 attenuated ferroptosis-associated vulnerability by reducing intracellular reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, CWH43 promoted redox-adaptive programs involving activation of NRF2-dependent antioxidant signaling, upregulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, increased intracellular glutathione availability, and suppression of lipid peroxidation. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of SLC7A11 restored ferroptosis susceptibility and sensitized CWH43-overexpressing colorectal cancer cells to therapeutic stress, whereas ferrostatin-1 partially restored cell viability following erastin-containing treatments. Collectively, these findings identify CWH43 as a regulator of redox adaptation that modulates ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer, providing insights into stress-adaptive survival mechanisms and chemotherapy resistance in cancer cells.

articles.title: Folate metabolism in tumor-associated macrophages drives immunosuppressive function to promote tumor growth.
articles.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) promote tumor growth, inhibit effector lymphocytes, and induce resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). Therapies designed to deplete TAMs have had little success in the clinic, and strategies aimed to repolarize immunosuppressive TAMs to pro-inflammatory states have struggled with systemic toxicity. articles.title: Incidence, burden, and associated factors of severe potential drug-drug interactions in intensive care unit patients: a real-world retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Severe potential drug-drug interactions (pDDIs) in intensive care unit (ICU) patients remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the incidence, patterns, burden, and associated factors of severe pDDIs.
